3.1ElementsofWeather/Climate
Weather/climatic elements are parameters which help to specify the weather/climate of a
place or region, such as air temperature, atmospheric pressure, winds and precipitation.
I. Atmospheric temperature: The atmospheric temperature refers to degree of heat in the air.
It is measured with a thermometer. Temperature is represented on maps by lines known as
isotherms. Temperature is most important climatic element. The temperature of a place is
primarily dependent on its distance from equator, the altitude and the prevailing winds.
ii.
Atmospheric pressure: Atmospheric Pressure refers to the weight of the air over a place. It
is measured with a barometer and is expressed in millibars (mb). It is represented on maps
by Isobars. Atmospheric pressure has a direct impact on the precipitation. In general,
places with low pressure tend to be moist, whereas those with high pressure are dry.
ii. Wind: The horizontal movement of air is termed as wind. Its direction is measured with a
wind vane, while anemometer is used to measure its speed. Winds transport heat and
moisture.
iv. Precipitation: The water that falls from the clouds is termed as precipitation. Precipitation
is measuredwitharain guage,Quantity of precipitation is represented on mapsby Isohyets.
